methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $10M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 12 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

methods.name: Public-Comp Anchoring
methods.skip_reason: target revenue not on file (private companies rarely disclose)
methods.rationale: Public Semiconductors P/S median is 21.5x across 3 tickers. Cannot apply without target's revenue.

data.narrative:
Lab 91 is a seed-stage semiconductor company founded by Anand Chamarthy that has raised $10M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a broader comp universe of 3 public semiconductor names (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers including Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, and Etched, though same-stage and narrow-filter comparables proved insufficient for direct peer median pricing.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable lens here. Using the $10M raised as a valuation proxy and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from Seed to Series A yields an implied valuation of $25M. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied without disclosed revenue; the semiconductor sector median P/S of 21.5x across the three public comps is calculable but not actionable for a pre-revenue or undisclosed-revenue entity. Peer-median triangulation was rejected due to insufficient same-stage or narrow-tier comparables within the semiconductor sector—only 1 adjacent-stage peer emerged after filtering, well below the 3-datapoint minimum for statistical reliability.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $21M to $29M, centered on $25M. This range reflects modest downside and upside around the stage-progression result, but the conclusion rests on a single method. Key uncertainties include the absence of direct peer valuation data, no revenue baseline for public-comp work, and limited visibility into Lab 91's specific technical differentiation relative to the broader private-company peer set.
